examples.question_text:
(a) $\$1200$ earns $5\%$ p.a. for $3$ years. Compare simple interest with annual compounding: how much extra interest does compounding earn, to the nearest cent?
(b) What is the difference if the same investment is held for only one year?
examples.solution_text:
(a) $I=Prn$.
$I=1200\times0.05\times3$.
$I=\$180$.
$FV=PV(1+r)^n$.
$FV=1200(1.05)^3$.
$FV=\$1389.15$.
Compound interest $=1389.15-1200$.
Compound interest $=\$189.15$.
Extra interest $=189.15-180$.
Extra interest $=\$9.15$.
(b) Simple interest $=1200\times0.05\times1$.
Simple interest $=\$60$.
Compound interest $=1200(1.05)-1200$.
Compound interest $=\$60$.
Difference $=60-60$.
Difference $=\$0$.

examples.question_text: A deposit of $\$3600$ can earn $8\%$ p.a. simple interest with $A$, or $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually with $B$. Compare their final balances (a) after $3$ years and (b) after $6$ years. Give each winning margin to the nearest cent.
$\$1800$ is invested for $3$ years at $10\%$ p.a. Complete the yearly ending balances for simple interest and annual compound interest.
examples.solution_text:
Simple interest each year $=1800\times0.10$.
Simple interest each year $=\$180$.
Simple ending balance, year $1$: $1800+180=\$1980$.
Simple ending balance, year $2$: $1980+180=\$2160$.
Simple ending balance, year $3$: $2160+180=\$2340$.
Compound interest, year $1$: $1800\times0.10=\$180$.
Compound ending balance, year $1$: $1800+180=\$1980$.
Compound interest, year $2$: $1980\times0.10=\$198$.
Compound ending balance, year $2$: $1980+198=\$2178$.
Compound interest, year $3$: $2178\times0.10=\$217.80$.
Compound ending balance, year $3$: $2178+217.80=\$2395.80$.

$A$ is the simple interest account: its graph is a straight line.
Simple interest each year $=2000\times0.10=\$200$.
$B$ is the compound interest account: its graph curves upwards and gets steeper.
Compound interest, year $1$: $2000\times0.10=\$200$.
Compound ending balance, year $1$: $2000+200=\$2200$.
Compound interest, year $2$: $2200\times0.10=\$220$.
Compound ending balance, year $2$: $2200+220=\$2420$.
Compound interest, year $3$: $2420\times0.10=\$242$.
The compound account adds a larger amount of interest each year.

examples.question_text: $\$4800$ earns $6.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually for $4$ years. Find the simple annual rate that earns the same total interest over those years, to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Compound interest $I=4800(1.065)^4-4800$.
For the same interest, $I=4800\times r\times4$.
$r=\dfrac{4800(1.065)^4-4800}{4800\times4}$.
As a percentage, $r\approx7.16\%$ p.a. Keep the unrounded compound interest when dividing.

examples.question_text:
Two accounts each start with $\$4000$ at $5\%$ p.a. Their yearly ending balances are shown below. Find which account has the greater balance after year $3$, and by how much.

| Year | Simple interest | Annual compound interest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $\$4200.00$ | $\$4200.00$ |
| $2$ | $\$4400.00$ | $\$4410.00$ |
| $3$ | $\$4600.00$ | $\$4630.50$ |
examples.solution_text:
Read the two balances in the year $3$ row.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4630.50-4600.00\\&=30.50\end{aligned}$

The compound account has the greater balance, by $\$30.50$.

methods.description: Calculate simple interest and its final balance, calculate annually compounded future value and interest, then compare.
